what: The epistemological framework and vocabulary of Dignāga's and Dharmakīrti's school - the particular and the conceptual, exclusion (apoha/apohana), self-awareness, causal efficacy - taken up by Utpaladeva and turned against the no-self thesis.

evidence.detail: ĪPK 1.2 states the Buddhist objection as pūrvapakṣa
apohana as one of the Lord's powers (ĪPK 1.3.7, 1.6.5)

notes: Coverage map C lists this borrowing; U49 may record it under another id - to be deduplicated at merge.

what: Bhartṛhari's doctrine that awareness is inherently verbal (vāc) and of the levels of speech, reworked as vimarśa = supreme speech, while paśyantī is denied ultimacy.

evidence.detail: Śivadṛṣṭi 2 refutes the grammarians by name

what: The Kaula ritual and doctrine (kula/akula, the Kula worship, the Kaula lineages) integrated by Abhinavagupta, taught him by Śambhunātha of Jālandhara.
The Krama's twelve Kālīs and Kālasaṅkarṣiṇī, integrated as a form of the śākta means and as the fourth goddess above the Trika triad.
Kṣemarāja's fusion of Spanda and Pratyabhijñā: spanda read as vimarśa and svātantrya; the Spandakārikā commented on in the light of the Pratyabhijñā.
The ritual framework of the Mantramārga - initiation and consecration procedures, the thirty-six tattvas, the three impurities, Śiva's five acts, śaktipāta - adopted and reinterpreted non-dually.

evidence.detail: Tantrāloka chs. 14-28 on initiation and rites
Shared ritual system of the Mantramārga

what: Sāṃkhya's twenty-five principles incorporated as tattvas 12-36 of the thirty-six.

evidence.detail: Paramārthasāra 19-22 lists prakṛti, the inner organ, senses, subtle and gross elements in Sāṃkhya order

what: The prakāśa-vimarśa metaphysics and Spanda/Pratyabhijñā exegesis used in Śrīvidyā commentary (Jayaratha's Vāmakeśvarīmatavivaraṇa; Maheśvarānanda; the Kāmakalāvilāsa).
Abhinavagupta's aesthetics - rasa as the relishing (carvaṇā) of consciousness, śānta as a rasa - drawing on his Śaiva doctrine.
A Kashmiri Vaiṣṇava (Bhagavadutpala) comments on the Spandakārikā, reading it alongside Pāñcarātra sources.
Abhinavagupta's Paramārthasāra recasts the older Paramārthasāra / Ādhārakārikā ascribed to Ādiśeṣa 'by the view of Śiva's teaching'.
